label: Research & evidence
title: Start with the question.
brand: Win Theory / Aarti / The Product Report
detail: I research the subject and the audience before choosing a treatment. I look at the original campaign or product, check dates and comparisons, and keep claims separate from opinions. A useful brief carries the question, the evidence, the image that explains it and the person checking it. For a product test, the method and the actual purchased sample matter as much as the script.

label: Personal brands
title: Give them a reason to return.
lines: A point of view. A recognisable voice.
detail: A personal brand starts with what this person can explain or do that people want to return for. I connect expertise to a recognisable voice, recurring formats and visual habits. Aarti’s marketing explanations, Mumbai interactions, two-character debates and square nostalgia format do different jobs. I research the example first, leave room for her interpretation and natural reactions, then compare the formats by viewing behaviour, shares, profile visits and follows.

label: Brand & campaign strategy
title: Work out the promise.
detail: I map the audience’s questions, the buying objection and what the brand can actually support. For TruNativ, education, creator demonstrations, founder answers and a premium product film have different roles. Everyday and Marine Collagen need distinct messages and identities. I connect the angle, offer, script and landing-page promise, then set a test that can tell us what to change.

label: Channel & content playbooks
title: Make the next one easier.
lines: Build a system around the show.
detail: I research how the audience uses the format before writing the edit rules. A recipe needs action and outcome; an identity film needs complete statements; a conversation needs the real setup and response. The playbook turns that into repeatable commissions, source logs, graphic triggers, caption rules, packaging and review gates. It gives the next editor a usable system without forcing every channel into the same pacing or visual language.

label: Packaging & brand identity
title: Build one clear system.
lines: From the shelf to the screen.
detail: I work out the reading order before fitting artwork to a real structure. Brand, product, flavour, information panels and code areas have different jobs. The packaging documents connect the vendor dieline, SKU copy, editable lettering, colour proof and print handoff. The same approved label becomes the render texture, so the physical pack, product page and CGI film recognise one product. I test the hierarchy at print size, shelf distance and phone scale.

label: Writing & storyboards
title: Work out the film first.
lines: A board that connects to the shoot.
detail: I turn the strategy into a premise, script and visible action. Each scene earns its place: what the viewer learns, what the camera must see and what the edit needs next. Zoho’s office movement, Sweet’s household comedy, Alanna’s product explanation and Collagen’s CG argument need different boards. These are paired with dialogue, shot instructions, continuity and review notes, so the drawings lead to usable footage and renders.

label: Shoot planning & teams
title: Plan for the edit.
detail: I plan the shoot around the finished explanation or performance. That means coverage, eyelines, sound, lighting, prop resets, product holds and protection takes before choosing extra movement. I group setups, assign owners and schedule the dependencies: research approval before procurement, rehearsal before trials, results before pickups. The team gets the brief, scene and take IDs, continuity records, selected material and clear delivery requirements.

label: VFX briefs & shot planning
title: Brief the shot before the effect.
brand: Win Theory / Creator Engine / Marine Collagen
artifact: Generation briefs, shot sheets & CG gates
detail: I separate the shot’s purpose from the technique used to make it. The brief names the reference, action, camera constraint, light direction, plate and forbidden changes. I plan clean plates, interaction, tracking needs and cut handles with production. CG starts from the real pack and approved label; AI starts from identity and continuity references. The review gates protect the premise before anyone spends time on final polish.

label: Edit strategy & retention
title: Find the shape of this film.
lines: Research the format. Log the source.
detail: I look at the title promise, audience behaviour, comparable formats and the actual source before deciding how to cut. I log missing context, repeated setup, premature reveals and reaction mismatches. An interview, game, recipe and verification film each need a different structure. I review the dialogue or explanation first, then refine the opening, pacing, evidence and payoff. Retention findings become specific changes for the next brief.

label: Identity & motion systems
title: Make the information readable.
brand: The Product Report / Hizzouse / Win Theory
detail: I connect motion to the thought being explained: object, relevant detail, comparison, then a readable hold. The identity becomes reusable source panels, lower thirds, chapter cards, rankings and caption rules. Each cue has approved copy, a source, a trigger and a version. Editable text, layered artwork and safe-area checks keep the next episode efficient and the information clear at phone size.

label: AI, VFX & finishing
title: Make it belong in the shot.
detail: I judge the full moving shot, not just the best frame. The review checks identity, anatomy, camera, light, motion, contact and neighbouring shots. A local defect can be repaired; a failed action or face turn needs a different performance or shot. Accepted material travels with its reference version, colour, frame rate, matte, plate and cut handles. The same discipline carries the film through graphics, sound, grading and delivery.

label: Testing & the next brief
title: Use the result. Change the brief.
artifact: Creative tests, format review & case proof
detail: I define the question and the decision rule before a test starts. I keep dates, audience, duration, distribution and spend with the result, then compare like-for-like work. Reach, viewing behaviour, qualified enquiries and purchases tell us different things. I connect the finding to one next change: a hook, explanation, performer, format or offer. That closes the loop back into research and commissioning.
